findings.title: Reader thread is never joined, so the assertion races with in-flight reads
findings.body: createMultiDeleteMultiReadMulti() starts a background thread that loops until deletedAll is set, then the main thread sets deletedAll.set(true) and immediately asserts caughtExceptions is empty without joining the thread. The reader thread can still be inside groups() when the assertion runs; an exception thrown by that final in-flight iteration is added to caughtExceptions after the assertion has already passed, so the regression this test is meant to catch can be silently missed (false positive). The thread should be joined before asserting.

findings.title: Shared admin client used concurrently from two threads can produce unrelated failures
findings.body: The reader thread and the main thread both use managedRealm.admin() (the same injected admin client / realm resource) concurrently. Keycloak's admin client is not thread-safe with respect to token refresh, so this test can fail intermittently for reasons unrelated to the NPE being fixed (e.g., concurrent token refresh errors recorded in caughtExceptions), making it flaky in CI. Consider using a separate admin client instance in the reader thread.

findings.title: getSubGroupsCount() now returns null for a deleted group, risking NPE in callers that unbox the Long
findings.body: The fix replaces the NPE inside getSubGroupsCount() with 'return model == null ? null : model.getSubGroupsCount();'. While GroupRepresentation.setSubGroupCount accepts null, any other caller that unboxes the returned Long (e.g., arithmetic or comparison on getSubGroupsCount()) will now get a NullPointerException exactly in the concurrent-deletion scenario this PR is addressing. Other group model implementations never return null here (they return the actual count or 0), so returning 0 (or the cached subgroup set size) would preserve the contract more safely.
